attorneys.name: Laura C. McGuire
attorneys.practice_type: Corporate & Commercial Lawyers in Des Moines, IA
attorneys.bio:
Laura is the chair of Belin McCormick’s banking department. She represents banks and businesses in corporate and regulatory matters.

She is known, first and foremost, for representing Iowa banks. She regularly counsels banks and other financial institutions through mergers and acquisitions, regulatory applications, and federal and state compliance matters. Her experience in the banking sector allows her to help clients navigate a complex regulatory environment with clarity and confidence.

Additionally, Laura maintains a corporate practice that spans the full lifecycle of business operations. She assists corporate clients with entity formation and structuring, corporate governance, contract negotiation, and strategic growth through mergers and acquisitions.

Laura’s business and banking clients benefit from her integrated practice, which allows her to combine corporate and banking expertise to advise on a wide range of commercial transactions.

Earlier in her career, Laura was privileged to serve as chief counsel to a U.S. District Court Judge in the Southern District of Iowa. Additionally, prior to joining Belin McCormick, Laura gained valuable insight practicing with banking and corporate attorneys at two other preeminent Des Moines firms. Her time with the District Court makes her uniquely suited to advise clients on transactional matters with litigation risk, and her experience with other practitioners makes her a valuable resource for what’s market in Iowa.

attorneys.name: Todd Miler
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in West Des Moines, IA
attorneys.bio:
Todd grew up on the Southside of Des Moines, attending Lincoln High School. He attended the University of Northern Iowa, graduating with a double major of Marketing and Spanish. He then attended Drake University Law School, earning a Juris Doctorate. He has been practicing criminal law since 1997. He has successfully defended cases through jury trial in many counties throughout the State of Iowa, including cases of murder, kidnapping, sexual abuse, robbery, drugs and OWI. He has been able to get murder charges dropped on two occasions prior to trial through a vigorous investigation of the facts and knowledge of the law. Through this experience he has developed a network of consultants, investigators and forensic experts to assist in the representation of his clients. Todd believes that an experienced team approach to a case, involving not only all the attorneys at Lombardi and Miler, but involving input from those experts where appropriate, provides the best defense.

He is passionate about defending the Constitution and the rights provided to all persons. In our system, a criminal defense attorney is the person responsible for maintaining liberty through a fair process. A criminal defense attorney needs to zealously defend each and every case, otherwise the government can run unchecked over the rights of our people.

In the civil arena, he has also successfully litigated and tried to juries cases involving medical malpractice, personal injury and wrongful death.

Todd is an avid hunter and outdoor enthusiast. He has also completed marathons in more than 20 states, and ultramarathons of 50 miles in several states, including Colorado, Wyoming and Minnesota.

attorneys.name: Cristy Tackett
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Davenport, IA
attorneys.bio:
Cristy Tackett-Hunt helps families and business owners preserve, protect and transfer their wealth by developing tax-efficient estate plans and business structures that both accomplish client goals and minimize risk.

As part of her estate planning practice, Cristy counsels individuals and families with modest to substantial assets, professionals in all stages of their careers and business owners. She cooperates with each client’s trusted advisors to understand their particular needs and objectives and, then employs a variety of tools to design the appropriate estate and asset protection plans, including simple and sophisticated revocable (living) and irrevocable trusts, wills, and powers of attorney. Cristy also assists individual clients with pre- and post-marital agreements, business clients with issues relating to succession planning including buy-sell agreements and fiduciaries (trustees and executors) on matters relating to trust and estate administration. She is a member of WealthCounsel, a national organization of top estate planning attorneys, financial advisors and insurance professionals.

In her business law practice, Cristy assists clients in identifying and forming an appropriate entity – whether that is a corporation, limited liability company, or partnership – or constructing a more sophisticated organizational structure. She further advises clients on issues relating to owner agreements, organizational governance, business transactions and dissolutions.

Cristy has been in private practice since 2006 and in June, 2012 founded the Law Offices of Cristy Tackett-Hunt PLLC. Cristy has also served as in-house counsel to a private trust company and personal legal counsel to its high net-worth clients, as a tax consultant and senior manager at Ernst & Young LLP, an international accounting firm and as an adjunct faculty member teaching “Law for Accounts” offered through the Master of Accounting program at St. Ambrose University.

attorneys.name: James Nelsen
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in West Des Moines, IA
attorneys.bio:
James Nelsen is a husband, father, avid football and baseball fan, and life experience enthusiast. He also happens to be a lawyer. His approachable nature and desire to help people provides representation that is intended to reduce the stress of your situation, but still ensure informative, insightful, and effective counsel. With the assistance of the team at Stowers and Nelsen, he provides client-centered, detailed, and results-driven counsel. From day one, James provides a roadmap for establishing the best defenses available, developing crucial facts, and analyzing legal issues involved in your matter. In cooperation with you from your initial strategy session, he will provide comprehensive and relentless representation.

James's journey to practicing law came by way of the University of Iowa and Dana College, where he earned his earned his Bachelor's degree in Sociology in 1998 with a minor in Psychology. Following graduation, he took a job with an insurance company in Des Moines, handling injury claims, managing coverage questions, and negotiating loss settlements with claimants, gaining valuable real-world experience. Disillusioned in his daily efforts, James developed a desire to be in the corner of the little guy and make sure good people better understood the totality of their circumstance.

Always having been determined to be a lawyer, his experience in the insurance industry strengthened his resolve. In 2000, James made it his mission to go to law school. He returned home from work one day, ordered the Law School Admission Test materials and enrollment packet, and registered to sit for the L.S.A.T. After he received his exam results, he was admitted to Drake Law School. In the fall of 2001, he resigned from his position in the insurance company and enrolled at Drake Law School. While in Law School he was a member of the Moot Court Board, represented criminal clients as a Student Attorney in the Legal Clinic, and was a member of the ATLA Mock Trial Team for two years. The team placed second nationally in his final year. He earned his J.D. in the Spring of 2004.

Following the 2004 summer bar exam, he was admitted by the Iowa Supreme Court to practice in Iowa, admitted to Federal District court in 2005, the Eight Circuit Court of Appeals in 2008, and Missouri in 2012. Relying upon his legal knowledge, litigation skills and techniques, and his personal passion and life experience, he provides quality legal service to people across Iowa. He has dedicated his practice to representing good people who have found themselves in bad situations. He persistently pursues the best outcomes and best results for people based upon their circumstance. He helps you strategically and methodically address issues and resolve problems. Whether you have been accused of a crime that could cost your reputation, livelihood, or freedom, or you are attempting to navigate a criminal investigation, he handles your problems effectively while answering questions and providing sound legal counsel. He listens, offers his guidance, and provides you with effective and skilled representation. He is dedicated to providing forthright, quality advocacy and is committed to achieving the best outcome possible for every client he accepts.

James has handled in excess of a thousand criminal cases, including high profile criminal matters and various personal injury matters across Iowa and in Missouri. He has successfully litigated cases in State and Federal court, including complex multiple party litigation, high profile murder and kidnapping cases, and international drug conspiracies. With his results focused approach to criminal matters, legal knowledge and life experience, James brings a comprehensive method to case management, and provides a resolve which is evidenced by a proven track record of success. In his representation of you, James will provide honest and forthright advice as well as outstanding advocacy.

If you have questions and want answers about criminal allegations or if you are the subject of a criminal investigation and want to know your options, contact James to set up a strategy session.

UNIQUELY QUALIFIED TO DEFEND YOU

- Successfully litigated high profile homicide, kidnapping, and drug offenses involving mandatory life sentences, and maintains the distinction of never having had a client receive a life sentence.

- Regularly attends national training seminars to remain knowledgeable of the latest and most cutting-edge legal issues

- Awarded 2016 Top Ten in Iowa Criminal Defense

WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT FROM REPRESENTATION

- Maxim: to craft a defense, you must know how to deconstruct a case, factually and legally. To deconstruct a case, you must know how it is constructed.

- Provides straightforward, unfiltered case analysis and advice, doesn't make empty promises.

Represented a client in a State drug offense which ultimately proceeded to trial. sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
James Nelsen is a husband, father, avid football and baseball fan, and life experience enthusiast. He also happens to be a lawyer. His approachable nature and desire to help people provides representation that is intended to reduce the stress of your situation, but still ensure informative, insightful, and effective counsel. With the assistance of the team at Stowers and Nelsen, he provides client-centered, detailed, and results-driven counsel. From day one, James provides a roadmap for establishing the best defenses available, developing crucial facts, and analyzing legal issues involved in your matter. In cooperation with you from your initial strategy session, he will provide comprehensive and relentless representation.

James's journey to practicing law came by way of the University of Iowa and Dana College, where he earned his earned his Bachelor's degree in Sociology in 1998 with a minor in Psychology. Following graduation, he took a job with an insurance company in Des Moines, handling injury claims, managing coverage questions, and negotiating loss settlements with claimants, gaining valuable real-world experience. Disillusioned in his daily efforts, James developed a desire to be in the corner of the little guy and make sure good people better understood the totality of their circumstance.

Always having been determined to be a lawyer, his experience in the insurance industry strengthened his resolve. In 2000, James made it his mission to go to law school. He returned home from work one day, ordered the Law School Admission Test materials and enrollment packet, and registered to sit for the L.S.A.T. After he received his exam results, he was admitted to Drake Law School. In the fall of 2001, he resigned from his position in the insurance company and enrolled at Drake Law School. While in Law School he was a member of the Moot Court Board, represented criminal clients as a Student Attorney in the Legal Clinic, and was a member of the ATLA Mock Trial Team for two years. The team placed second nationally in his final year. He earned his J.D. in the Spring of 2004.

Following the 2004 summer bar exam, he was admitted by the Iowa Supreme Court to practice in Iowa, admitted to Federal District court in 2005, the Eight Circuit Court of Appeals in 2008, and Missouri in 2012. Relying upon his legal knowledge, litigation skills and techniques, and his personal passion and life experience, he provides quality legal service to people across Iowa. He has dedicated his practice to representing good people who have found themselves in bad situations. He persistently pursues the best outcomes and best results for people based upon their circumstance. He helps you strategically and methodically address issues and resolve problems. Whether you have been accused of a crime that could cost your reputation, livelihood, or freedom, or you are attempting to navigate a criminal investigation, he handles your problems effectively while answering questions and providing sound legal counsel. He listens, offers his guidance, and provides you with effective and skilled representation. He is dedicated to providing forthright, quality advocacy and is committed to achieving the best outcome possible for every client he accepts.

James has handled in excess of a thousand criminal cases, including high profile criminal matters and various personal injury matters across Iowa and in Missouri. He has successfully litigated cases in State and Federal court, including complex multiple party litigation, high profile murder and kidnapping cases, and international drug conspiracies. With his results focused approach to criminal matters, legal knowledge and life experience, James brings a comprehensive method to case management, and provides a resolve which is evidenced by a proven track record of success. In his representation of you, James will provide honest and forthright advice as well as outstanding advocacy.

If you have questions and want answers about criminal allegations or if you are the subject of a criminal investigation and want to know your options, contact James to set up a strategy session.

attorneys.practice_type: Administrative Law Lawyers in Clive, IA
attorneys.bio:
Trent focuses primarily on administrative law. As an attorney for Sellers, Galenbeck & Nelson, Trent has worked on a variety of cases dealing with a number of agencies, including the Iowa Board of Medicine, Iowa Board of Pharmacy, Iowa Board of Social Work, Iowa Board of Nursing, Iowa Board of Cosmetology, the Iowa Department of Health and Human Services, the Office of the Inspector General, the Internal Revenue Service, the Drug Enforcement Administration and many others.

A graduate of Iowa State University, Trent enjoys representing Midwestern clients and is proud to call Iowa his home. Trent is particularly interested in helping preserving the rights of individuals when government and corporate actors overstep their bounds.

attorneys.name: Michael T. Norris
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in West Des Moines, IA
attorneys.bio:
Mike attended grade school and high school in southwest Iowa graduating from South Page High School in 1994. He attended Graceland University in Lamoni, Iowa where he graduated with honors and was a member of the football and track teams. He then attended Drake University Law School where he graduated in 2002.

For the past 20 plus years, Mike has committed his legal practice to helping individuals and the families of those who have been victims of personal injury and medical practice. During this time attorney Norris has recovered millions of dollars in damages on behalf of individuals and families whose loved ones were severely injured or killed as a result of negligence or medical malpractice.

Mike has successfully tried cases obtaining jury verdicts all over Iowa in both state and federal courts and is currently licensed in all Iowa state district courts and in both the Northern and Southern Districts of federal court in Iowa. Mike has also successfully argued appeals in the Iowa Supreme Court and Iowa Court of Appeals.

Mike is married to Lori Norris and together they have five children. When away from the practice of law, Mike enjoys coaching his children and attending their sporting events. Mike and Lori are also avid motorcycle riders who take advantage of their rare free time by riding their Harley throughout Iowa with friends.

attorneys.name: Michael R. Reck
attorneys.practice_type: Appeals Lawyers in Des Moines, IA
attorneys.bio:
Mike Reck is a shareholder of the firm who has handled a wide variety of litigation matters over the years ranging from complex commercial litigation to employment disputes. Mike assists clients in all stages of litigation from pre-litigation strategy, planning through summary judgment, trial, and defending appeals where necessary. Mike and those who work with him believe in a proactive approach to litigating cases designed to highlight the legal issues and to seek resolution through an appropriate motion.

Mike has extensive experience in large and complex litigation including representative suits such as proposed collective actions, class actions and derivative suits. That experience includes a vanishing premium class action in the insurance industry, a proposed class action challenging mortgage practices, asbestos property damage class actions, a proposed public nuisance class action, antitrust class actions, a shareholder fraud class action, Fair Labor Standards collective actions, and derivative suits challenging corporate mergers.

Mike also provides clients with substantial counseling in labor and employment matters. He assists clients with the full range of employee relations matters including drafting and editing employee handbooks and manuals, investigating employee allegations and complaints, representing clients before Iowa's Civil Rights Commission and the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, and counseling on compliance with the full range of regulatory matters including the WARN Act, the Family & Medical Leave Act, the ADA, the ADEA, Title VII and the Wage Payment Collection Act. Mr. Reck has been recognized by Chambers and Partners for his employment law practice.

Mark D. Reed has worked with the Marberry Law Firm, P.C. in Urbandale, Iowa since July of 2009. Previously he helped form the law firm of Reed & Epping, P.C. in October of 1997.

Mr. Reed practices in the areas of debt matters, small business, family and juvenile, criminal, and general will, small estate planning and probate. Mr. Reed is also a certified family law mediator. He also has experience in the area of appeals in both state and federal courts. Mr. Reed is licensed in the Iowa Supreme Court, the Federal Courts for the Northern and Southern District of Iowa and the federal Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals.

Mr. Reed has lectured for continuing legal education seminars provided to other lawyers in the State of Iowa in the areas of juvenile law and debtor/creditor law.

Mr. Reed is also a long standing member of the board of directors of a large Midwestern credit union with offices in Iowa, Illinois, Minnesota and Wisconsin whose mission is to serve the underserved.

attorneys.bio:

A Nebraska native, Taylor earned a degree in Political Science with a minor in Psychology from the University of Kearney - Nebraska. In 2019, Taylor graduated with honors from Drake University Law School, where he also served as the article editor for the Drake Journal of Agricultural Law.

With five years of diverse legal experience, Taylor has a proven track record in the courtroom, having handled over a thousand cases. Taylor's expertise spans a wide range of criminal law, including violent crimes, drug offenses, felonies, and federal crimes. Additionally, Taylor is well-versed in employment discrimination cases and personal injury claims, bringing a comprehensive approach to client advocacy.

An experienced litigator, Taylor is known for his extensive trial experience and unwavering commitment to justice. Outside the courtroom, Taylor enjoys spending quality time with his two fluffy dogs, Hudson and Bear.

attorneys.name: Amanda M. Richards
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Davenport, IA
attorneys.bio:
Amanda Richards has practiced in the area of civil litigation since 2003. Originally from Princeton, Illinois, she attended Illinois College and Drake University Law School where she graduated with honors. While attending law school, Amanda worked in the legal department of an insurance company learning all aspects of insurance defense. It was through this experience that Amanda discovered her passion for defense litigation and her drive to be a strong voice for her clients during the litigation process.

Amanda practices in all areas of civil litigation, specializing in personal injury, medical/pharmaceutical malpractice, insurance bad faith, traumatic brain injury, premises liability, dram shop, labor/employment law, insurance coverage, declaratory actions, and unemployment matters. In 2020, she was inducted into the Iowa Academy of Trial Lawyers. She served as the President of the Iowa Defense Counsel Association from 2023-2024 and is currently on the Board of Governors of the Iowa Academy of Trial Lawyers.

Amanda is an avid writer and specializes in all stages of motion and appellate practice from administrative appeals, unemployment appeals, and litigation appeals to the state and federal appellate courts. She has argued in front of the Iowa and Illinois Appellate courts. She often teaches and presents at seminars and conferences sharing cutting edge techniques in discovery, trial tactics, and employment law matters.

Outside the courtroom Amanda resides in Bettendorf with her husband, Todd, their three children, Jocelyn, Hayden, and Landon. She is active in her community volunteering through the Pleasant Valley Community School District and serving as a handler to her two therapy dogs (Skylar and Remy) through Quad Cities Canine Assistance Network (QCCAN).

attorneys.name: Nicholas A. Sarcone
attorneys.practice_type: Assault & Domestic Assault Lawyers in Des Moines, IA
attorneys.bio:
If you are facing federal or state criminal charges you deserve your best defense.

Choosing a lawyer is a big deal. Your liberty is in our hands. Whether you have been caught in a bad circumstance or made a series of bad decisions, I have seen it before and you don’t have to face it alone. I will put my experience of representing thousands of people in state and federal criminal court to work for you and I intend to get you the best possible result.

When I worked at the Federal Public Defender’s Office while in law school at the University of Iowa, I had the realization that no matter the crime, everyone deserves a skilled, intelligent advocate working tirelessly to give them their best defense. If I were charged with a crime I would expect that, so why shouldn’t you? I believe that every person deserves the best possible defense. You are probably nervous, worried, scared and likely angry. That is natural. You want someone to deal with the problem and help you get the best outcome. That’s where I come in.

After my summers in the Federal Defender Office in San Francisco and the Federal Defender Office in Des Moines, I became an Assistant Public Defender in Tampa, FL. For the last several years I have been in private practice. I’ve represented thousands of clients facing charges ranging from simple assault to complex federal drug conspiracies to sexual assault, burglary, robbery and beyond. I’ve taken many of those clients to jury and bench trials. I have also argued some of their cases before the Iowa Supreme Court and Iowa Court of Appeals. It is likely that I have handled a case not unlike yours.

WHAT TO EXPECT

When I represent you, you can expect me to: communicate, counsel and advocate.

Communication. Communication is the key to any good relationship. Yes, I am busy. It is my intention to return phone calls and emails as quickly as possible. I also make it a priority to explain issues in your case and break them down so you understand them. Let’s face it, the law isn’t simple or easy (that’s why I went to law school) and that is why I am here.

Counsel. They don’t call us counselors for nothing. I am a straight shooter. I’m going to give you the most well reasoned advice I can give, even if you dislike it. I often counsel clients about steps they can take while their case is pending–to better themselves and their case. My job is to counsel you to the best outcome, whatever that may be.

Advocate. My job is to dig into your case and make sure no stone is left unturned. No record left unsubpoenaed. No motion left unfiled. Getting great plea deals, winning motions to suppress and getting cases dismissed requires creativity, skill and ingenuity in the approach to your defense. This becomes particularly important in trial or if I need to take your case before the Iowa Supreme Court.

Choosing a lawyer is a big deal. Your liberty is in our hands. It can be an overwhelming experience. While I cannot promise you what the outcome of your case will be, I can promise that I will put my experience and dedication to work for you. I look forward to your call!

After my summers in the Federal Defender Office in San Francisco and the Federal Defender Office in Des Moines, I became an Assistant Public Defender in Tampa, FL. For the last several years I have been in private practice. I’ve represented thousands of clients facing charges ranging from simple assault to complex federal drug conspiracies to sexual assault, burglary, robbery and beyond. I’ve taken many of those clients to jury and bench trials. I have also argued some of their cases before the Iowa Supreme Court and Iowa Court of Appeals. It is likely that I have handled a case not unlike yours.

WHAT TO EXPECT

When I represent you, you can expect me to: communicate, counsel and advocate.

Communication. Communication is the key to any good relationship. Yes, I am busy. It is my intention to return phone calls and emails as quickly as possible. I also make it a priority to explain issues in your case and break them down so you understand them. Let’s face it, the law isn’t simple or easy (that’s why I went to law school) and that is why I am here.

Counsel. They don’t call us counselors for nothing. I am a straight shooter. I’m going to give you the most well reasoned advice I can give, even if you dislike it. I often counsel clients about steps they can take while their case is pending–to better themselves and their case. My job is to counsel you to the best outcome, whatever that may be.

Advocate. My job is to dig into your case and make sure no stone is left unturned. No record left unsubpoenaed. No motion left unfiled. Getting great plea deals, winning motions to suppress and getting cases dismissed requires creativity, skill and ingenuity in the approach to your defense. This becomes particularly important in trial or if I need to take your case before the Iowa Supreme Court.

Choosing a lawyer is a big deal. Your liberty is in our hands. It can be an overwhelming experience. While I cannot promise you what the outcome of your case will be, I can promise that I will put my experience and dedication to work for you. I look forward to your call!

attorneys.name: Matthew G. Sease
attorneys.practice_type: Trial Law Lawyers in Des Moines, IA
attorneys.bio:
Matthew G. Sease is a highly accomplished trial and appellate attorney with a depth of experience and many successes in high‑stakes litigation. Matt has tried 25 jury trials and numerous bench trials across Iowa and in federal courts, achieving not‑guilty verdicts, multimillion‑dollar civil awards, complete defense verdicts, and significant wins in complex commercial, criminal, probate, and construction matters. His broad litigation experience, representing both plaintiffs and defendants, spans everything from first‑degree murder to multimillion‑dollar business disputes, reflecting a rare versatility and command of the courtroom.

Matt’s appellate practice is equally distinguished. He has handled over 70 appeals and has delivered over 30 oral arguments before the Iowa Supreme Court, Iowa Court of Appeals, the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals, and the Seventh Circuit Court of Appeals—often in cases involving issues of first impression or significant statewide importance. His ability to distill complex legal questions and advocate effectively at the appellate level has repeatedly led to reversals, precedent‑setting rulings, and favorable outcomes for his clients.

Widely recognized by his peers, Matt is a member of several invitation‑only organizations, including the prestigious American College of Trial Lawyers, American Board of Trial Advocates, and the Iowa Academy of Trial Attorneys—honors reserved for a small percentage of attorneys statewide. He has also been selected to Super Lawyers and named to the Million Dollar Advocates Forum.. No matter the case, Matt is known for his meticulous preparation, strategic insight, and unwavering advocacy, providing clients with clarity, confidence, and results when the stakes are highest.

attorneys.name: Michael M. Sellers
attorneys.practice_type: Licensing Board Defense Lawyers in Clive, IA
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Mike Sellers has been a fixture on the Iowa legal landscape for more than 45 years. Early in his career, the citizens of Mahaska County elected Mike as their county attorney where he acted as a prosecutor and advised County officials on legal affairs while cultivating his own practice alongside Bob Spayde and Jim Rielly in Oskaloosa, Iowa.

Soon, however, Mike left private practice when he was hand-picked by Governor Robert D. Ray to serve as one of the former governor’s staff attorneys. In this role, Mike worked with Governor Ray on a day-to-day basis, handling matters on the Governor’s behalf and acting as the Governor’s liaison to more than a dozen state agencies. In 1971, Governor Ray appointed Mike to serve as Public Safety Commissioner where he was responsible for statewide law enforcement and safety matters. In the wake of the Kent State shootings in 1970, Mike oversaw the implementation of the first 28E intergovernmental agency agreement in the nation which allowed the Iowa Department of Public Safety to coordinate the activities of multiple local, state and federal law enforcement agencies to ensure that no such tragedy would strike Iowa’s universities. In his role as Public Safety Commissioner, Mike was asked to join a panel at the Riverside College of Law at the University of California to address the appropriate exercise of police power in tumultuous times. He served on that panel with such names as renowned defense attorney F. Lee Bailey and “The King of Torts” Melvin Belli.

Leaving the public sector in 1973, Mike sought to use his experience and skill to protect individuals’ right against government abuses. Mike first became involved with agency law in 1973 and in the 1990s, he narrowed his practice to concentrate primarily on licensing board defense. Every day, Mike offers his guidance to healthcare professionals facing peer review or sanctions by hospitals, medical groups or state and federal agencies. Mike takes pride in exposing false and unfounded claims against physicians and other medical professionals and in demonstrating how his clients’ rights have been violated. Mike knows how pervasive competition is in and among specialty groups and other practices, and he has protected numerous clients who have been threatened with having their reputations tarnished.

Mike obtained his law degree from the University of Iowa College of Law. He is licensed to practice law in Iowa and is an active member of the Iowa State Bar Association, the Iowa Association of Justice and the Polk County Bar Association.

He has been active in Bar Association activities at the local, state and national level. From 2000 to 2006 he served on the Board of Governors of the Iowa State Bar Association and served as Chair of its Commercial and Bankruptcy Law Section from 2008 to 2011. He has also served as a Bankruptcy Trustee for over thirty-five years. He is married and has three adult children. He is active in his community having served as Mayor and on the Council Bluffs City Council.

Most recently, he has served as Chair of the Iowa West Foundation, the largest philanthropic foundation in western Iowa, from 2008 through 2012.

attorneys.name: Paul Statler
attorneys.practice_type: Sex Crimes Lawyers in Des Moines, IA
attorneys.bio:
Paul Statler is a dedicated criminal defense attorney with a proven record of fighting for the rights of his clients in state and federal courts across Iowa. Since 2015, Paul has focused his practice on criminal defense and postconviction relief, representing clients in cases ranging from serious felony charges to complex appeals in state and federal jurisdictions. He brings the same level of preparation, strategic thinking, and relentless advocacy to every case—whether in the courtroom, at the negotiation table, or in written pleadings.

Paul is admitted to practice before the Iowa state courts, the U.S. District Courts for the Northern and Southern Districts of Iowa, and the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit. He earned his Juris Doctor from Drake University Law School, receiving academic awards in Criminal Procedure and Federal Income Tax Law. While in law school, Paul served as President of the American Constitution Society and gained extensive hands-on experience through the Neal and Bea Smith Criminal Defense Legal Clinic, the Low-Income Taxpayer Clinic, and a year-long internship with the Federal Public Defender’s Office.

Paul’s clients value his straightforward personality and counsel, meticulous preparation, and willingness to take on even the most challenging cases. He understands that behind every file is a real person whose future depends on the outcome, and he works tirelessly to secure the best possible results.

When he’s not in the courtroom, Paul can often be found engaging with the legal community, mentoring younger attorneys, or spending time with his wife and two ‘crazy’ sons. His diverse background and personal experience gives him a unique perspective on discipline, perseverance, and problem-solving.

Professional perspective:

Inspired by a statement from former Georgia Public Defender, Brett Willis:

People ask me what I do, and when I tell them I’m a criminal defense attorney they ask, “what does that mean?” Almost always, I tell them, “I defend people who are accused of, and charged with committing crimes.” After hearing that, they’ll usually ask “how can you defend those people?”

I tell them the truth about what I do; I tell them, "it's not about 'those people' - it’s about the sanctity of human liberty, and the cost of it if you want to take it. Every person deserves even the most basic level of respect and deserves their rights to be protected against the government that seeks to take them away."

attorneys.name: Terzo Steves
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in West Des Moines, IA
attorneys.bio:
Terzo was born and raised in Cortez, Colorado, near the Four Corners. He didn’t grow up in a big city or with a silver spoon—he grew up on a cattle ranch in the mountains, where hard work wasn’t optional; it was just life. Before he was a lawyer, he was up at dawn tending to livestock, putting in long days in the fields, and learning firsthand that no one hands you anything—you earn it.

Sports were his escape and his passion. He played basketball, football, and baseball, and later, he coached youth teams in baseball and basketball, passing on the lessons of teamwork, discipline, and resilience. Those same qualities carried him through earning undergraduate degrees in Economics and Business at Colorado State University. Then law school brought him to Iowa, where he attended Drake University and started building his career.

He didn’t take shortcuts. He put in the work and built a name for himself in criminal defense, juvenile law, and Child in Need of Assistance (CINA) cases. He’s not the type to sit behind a desk and push papers—he’s in the trenches, fighting for his clients. He’s earned the respect of judges and attorneys across Iowa, not by talking a big game but by showing up, negotiating hard, and delivering results. He knows how to relate to people, how to tell their stories, and most importantly, how to fight for them.

And when he’s not in the courtroom? You might find him at the office with his loyal dog, Oby, who has a knack for bringing comfort to those who need it most. Or maybe he’s around the table with his crew, diving into a game of Dungeons & Dragons. And if you’re a sports fan, you might have even heard him on air as a regular personality on The Rich Eisen Show, where he brings his trademark wit and insight to sports discussions, blending his passion for the game with his natural ability to connect with others.

He’s not just a lawyer—he’s an advocate, a fighter, and someone who understands what it means to struggle and come out stronger. If you need someone in your corner, he’s ready to go to battle for you.

attorneys.name: Sierra Meehan Strassberg
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Des Moines, IA
attorneys.bio:
"I take great pride in supporting clients emotionally during what can be an exceedingly difficult time in their lives. I aim to help clients reach an outcome that allows them to move forward peacefully."

Sierra Meehan Strassberg graduated from Grinnell College in 2010 before receiving her J.D. from Brooklyn Law School in 2018. She was admitted to practice law in the State of New York in 2019 before moving back to her home state, Iowa, where she was admitted to practice in 2020.

Prior to law school, Sierra worked in restaurant management in New York City. While still in law school as part of the Brooklyn Law School Employment Law Clinic, she advocated for clients seeking Unemployment Benefits and assisted clients with employment conflicts being mediated by the New York City Commission On Human Rights. She was awarded the Silver Pro Bono Award for over 500 hours of pro bono work. Sierra also served as co-president on the board of the Student Animal Legal Defense Fund.

Upon graduation, Sierra gravitated towards the area of family law. She worked at a matrimonial law firm in New York City assisting clients in high-stake, contentious divorces.

After being admitted to practice in Iowa, Sierra pursued training as a family law mediator. She is an active member of the American Bar Association, the Iowa State Bar Association, and the Polk County Bar Association.

In her free time, Sierra enjoys reading, films, gardening, exploring new restaurants and volunteering at the Animal Rescue League.

Attorney Adrienne Sula joined Hupy and Abraham in 2025. She brings 10 years of experience as a trial lawyer and 3 years in corporate compliance law. She earned her Juris Doctor from Drake University Law School in 2010 and is licensed to practice in Iowa (state and federal), Nebraska, Michigan, and Wyoming.

Attorney Sula is an active member of the Iowa State Bar Association, the Iowa Creditors Bar Association, and the Polk County Bar Association. She is also a member of the Iowa Association for Justice, National Trial Lawyers, and the National Creditors Bar Association.

She is committed to serving her community and participates in a variety of volunteer and outreach activities throughout Iowa. She has supported events such as the Good Guys Car Show in Des Moines and the Iowa State Fair. She has also represented the firm at community and professional events, including the “Books and Bricks for Belize” charity auction and the Iowa Association for Justice “Justice Cup” with fellow attorney Eric Schade.

Additionally, she has attended ABATE (American Bikers Aimed Toward Education) meetings, participated in the Iowa Association for Justice Workers’ Compensation Division, volunteered at the Big Brothers Big Sisters Thanksgiving event, and assisted with ABATE’s Christmas toy drive by coordinating the delivery of donated items to local children’s organizations.

In 2020, Attorney Sula was recognized as a Lawyer of Distinction in Collection Law for her excellence and professionalism. Since joining the firm in March 2025, she has recovered hundreds of thousands of dollars for her clients.

attorneys.name: Cristy Tackett
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Davenport, IA
attorneys.bio:
Cristy Tackett-Hunt helps families and business owners preserve, protect and transfer their wealth by developing tax-efficient estate plans and business structures that both accomplish client goals and minimize risk.

As part of her estate planning practice, Cristy counsels individuals and families with modest to substantial assets, professionals in all stages of their careers and business owners. She cooperates with each client’s trusted advisors to understand their particular needs and objectives and, then employs a variety of tools to design the appropriate estate and asset protection plans, including simple and sophisticated revocable (living) and irrevocable trusts, wills, and powers of attorney. Cristy also assists individual clients with pre- and post-marital agreements, business clients with issues relating to succession planning including buy-sell agreements and fiduciaries (trustees and executors) on matters relating to trust and estate administration. She is a member of WealthCounsel, a national organization of top estate planning attorneys, financial advisors and insurance professionals.

In her business law practice, Cristy assists clients in identifying and forming an appropriate entity – whether that is a corporation, limited liability company, or partnership – or constructing a more sophisticated organizational structure. She further advises clients on issues relating to owner agreements, organizational governance, business transactions and dissolutions.

Cristy has been in private practice since 2006 and in June, 2012 founded the Law Offices of Cristy Tackett-Hunt PLLC. Cristy has also served as in-house counsel to a private trust company and personal legal counsel to its high net-worth clients, as a tax consultant and senior manager at Ernst & Young LLP, an international accounting firm and as an adjunct faculty member teaching “Law for Accounts” offered through the Master of Accounting program at St. Ambrose University.

attorneys.name: Jeffrey P. Taylor
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Law Lawyers in Cedar Rapids, IA
attorneys.bio:
Born in 1962 in Waterloo, Iowa, Jeff Taylor grew up on a Northeast Iowa farm where he learned the value of hard work and the value of a dollar. Farming and working construction for his father's construction company molded Mr. Taylor into the lawyer he is today: practical, hardworking, caring and dedicated to those he represents.

The Managing Partner of Klinger, Robinson & Ford since 1998, Jeff graduated from the University of Iowa Colleges of Business with Honors, and from the University of Iowa College of Law with High Distinction. With more than 35 years of experience in commercial and bankruptcy law, Mr. Taylor frequently represents Debtors and Creditors in both complex and routine matters. He represented the petitioning creditors in the largest involuntary bankruptcy case ever successfully filed in Iowa: In Re Walterman Implement, Inc.

Civil trial work is also a large portion of Mr. Taylor's practice, including contract litigation, and family law cases. Sound, practical advice in these areas allows him to help his clients feel at ease during the process and see that there is a light at the end of the long, dark tunnel. In his spare time, he enjoys listening to live music and all forms of motor sports.

attorneys.name: Michael Taylor
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Des Moines, IA
attorneys.bio:
Michael Taylor received his Bachelor of Science in Criminology and Psychology, from the University of Wisconsin - Whitewater. Michael then studied at Drake University Law School, receiving his Juris Doctor degree in 2025, and was later admitted to the bar in the state of Iowa. In addition to his degree, Michael earned a certificate in Constitutional Law and Civil Rights.

Prior to attending law school, Michael worked as a legal assistant in the Chicago area, at a firm specializing in criminal defense.

While receiving his legal education, Michael clerked at Roxanne Conlin & Associates, P.C., assisting clients in the areas of civil and constitutional rights, employment discrimination, and personal injury. He also acted as a student attorney in Drake's Children's Rights Clinic, handling anything from guardianships to complex juvenile delinquency matters.

Upon graduation, Michael was offered to join the firm as an Associate Attorney. Michael represents clients in all areas of the firm, including personal injury, civil and constitutional rights, and employment discrimination.

Michael is a member of the Iowa State Bar Association and the Iowa Association for Justice. In his free time, Michael enjoys watching sports and playing with his dog.

attorneys.name: Barbara Kay Wallace
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Davenport, IA
attorneys.bio:
Barbara Wallace joined Betty, Neuman & NcMahon, P.L.C. in October 2019 as a Partner. Barb graduated from Augustana College in Rock Island, IL and the University of Iowa College of Law. During law school, Barb worked as a prosecuting intern for the Scott County Attorneys Office. After law school, she worked as an Assistant County Attorney in Linn County, Iowa before going to work for a law firm in Rock Island, Illinois first as an Associate and later as a Partner. She worked for an Iowa law firm for 2 years before she started her own law firm where she worked until joining the Betty law firm.

Barb's practice is primarily limited to Scott County, Iowa and Rock Island County, Illinois with the exception of mediation. Barb has concentrated her practice in the area of family law and has also practiced in criminal law and traffic defense since 1997. She completed ACR Nationally Approved 40-hour Family Law Mediation Training in April 2008 and has since maintained a successful mediation practice as well. She is a Court Approved Mediator for Child Custody Cases for the Fourteenth Judicial Circuit Court of Illinois. Barb has been a member of the Iowa State Bar & Scott County Bar Associations since 1997 and the Rock Island County Bar Association since 2016. She served as a member of the Scott County Bar Executive Council in 2003 and has served as a member of the Fee Dispute Committee since 2012. Barb served as a member of the 7th Judicial District of Iowa's Mediation Committee in 2011 and Informal Family Law Trial Pilot Project Committee from 2016-2017. She also served as a member of the Iowa Supreme Court Family Law Case Processing Reform Task Force ADR Work Group from 2015-2016.

Barb lives in Davenport, IA with her husband Chris and their two daughters, where she volunteers in the community and enjoys boating, camping, traveling and scuba diving.

He was a member of the University of Chicago Law Review. Before attending law school, Matt graduated cum laude in business administration and accounting from the University of Notre Dame. He then earned a Master of Accountancy at the University of Iowa. In 2009, Matt passed all four sections of the Uniform Certified Public Accountant Examination. Born and raised in Des Moines, Matt is a Dowling Catholic High School alumnus.

attorneys.name: Bryan P. Webber
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce & Family Law Lawyers in Des Moines, IA
attorneys.bio: Bryan was born and raised in eastern Iowa and attended the University of Iowa graduating in 2003 with a B.A. Political Science and a minor in Business Administration. He then moved to the Des Moines area while he attended Drake Law School and remained after graduating and passing the bar in 2006. In 2007, he passed the Illinois bar and was also admitted into the Southern District of Iowa in federal court. He is currently practicing throughout central and southern Iowa, especially in Polk, Warren and Marion Counties. Bryan initially practiced at another local firm before joining Carr & Wright in 2011, as he saw the opportunity to join a dynamic and growing firm. Bryan brings passion, energy and extensive knowledge of complex family and juvenile law issues. He understands the stresses that these situations place on the client and their families. His experience in litigating and settling highly charged family and juvenile law matters combined with his experiences as a mediator have given him the perspective and knowledge necessary to aid clients in securing the best outcomes. He takes great pride in being able to guide clients through what can be a very difficult process emotionally while ensuring that the client always knows that he will represent them in the manner they want. In addition to family and juvenile law, Bryan also specializes in criminal defense, mediation, appeals and Chapter 7 Bankruptcy. Bryan is happily married and resides in the Des Moines Metro area. Call Bryan today to schedule an appointment to discuss your legal matter.

attorneys.name: Jenny L. Weiss
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Dubuque, IA
attorneys.bio:
Background

I grew up in the tri-state area, born in Hazel Green, Wisconsin, and moved to Dubuque at nine years old. I graduated from Hempstead High School before attending the University of Iowa, where I graduated from the College of Law in 2007. Immediately after law school, I returned to Dubuque to be close to family and friends—and I’ve been here ever since.

I began my legal career at Fuerste, Carew, Juergens & Sudmeier, P.C., where I practiced for nearly two decades. In January 2026, I fulfilled a long-held dream and opened my own firm, Jenny L. Weiss, PLLC. Starting my own practice has been both exciting and deeply rewarding, and I am grateful for the opportunity to serve my clients in this new chapter.

My Approach

I understand that when clients come to me, they are often navigating unfamiliar territory during some of the most stressful times in their lives. My role is to guide you through that uncertainty with honesty, patience, and a steady hand. Every client is different, and I take the time to understand not just your case, but your individual needs and how you communicate best.

I believe in being straightforward with you—giving you the information you need to hear, even when it’s not what you hoped for. That candor, I’ve found, builds trust and leads to better outcomes. At the same time, I am committed to finding practical solutions and working toward resolution whenever possible. While I am confident in the courtroom and prepared to advocate vigorously on your behalf when litigation is necessary, I also value negotiation and know that the best result is often one that avoids prolonged conflict.

I genuinely enjoy the practice of law—from the give-and-take of negotiation to the precision of drafting appellate briefs. I have had the privilege of arguing before both the Iowa Supreme Court and the Iowa Court of Appeals, experiences I consider highlights of my career. What I love most about this work is that it is an art: there is always a way to craft a thoughtful argument or find a creative path forward. I thrive on that challenge and am always learning something new in this ever-evolving field.

Personal

In February 2026, my husband and I will celebrate fourteen years of marriage. I enjoy dinner nights with him and trying new restaurants—when I can convince him to be a little adventurous. Outside of work, you’ll find me reading, traveling, gardening in my backyard, or sharing strong drinks with good friends. My greatest joy in life is my nieces and nephews, whom I love to spoil rotten before happily handing them back to their parents.

attorneys.name: Thomas M. Wertz
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Cedar Rapids, IA
attorneys.bio:
Some lawyers dabble in many different areas of the law. Not so for Tom Wertz. Shortly after moving into private practice, he turned his focus to workers' compensation and representing injured workers. Wertz quickly recognized the need for experienced attorneys in this specialized field. His commitment has resulted in a legal practice representing injured workers for more than 35 years.

His record before the Iowa Supreme Court has led to major legal changes on behalf of injured workers. These changes include:

• Compensation benefits for tinnitus (ringing in the ears) and acute psychological injuries.

• Home medical care for out-of-state injured workers. These workers no longer have to travel to Iowa for care.

• Required reevaluations by insurance companies. They must now revisit denied claims when new information is received.

• Compensation cannot be reduced because of pre-existing limitations on employment.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Two Time recipient of the Verne Lawyer Outstanding Member Award

First ever Iowa Association for Justice Pac Champion
